title: Premium for Heightened Uncertainty: Explaining Pre-Announcement Market Returns
one_line: Large overnight market returns occur before nonfarm payrolls, ISM and GDP releases, similar to pre-FOMC returns and with no abnormal variance; they reflect the build-up and resolution of 'impact uncertainty' measured by VIX.

findings.statement: Large overnight returns before NFP, ISM and GDP announcements, similar to pre-FOMC.
No abnormal variance in those windows.
Returns tied to VIX build-up before and drop at the announcement (impact uncertainty).

why.pattern: Risk premium for heightened uncertainty about how much the news will move markets.
why.mechanism: Uncertainty builds before scheduled news, investors demand a premium, it resolves just before the release.

reported_results.headline: Positive pre-announcement overnight returns before NFP/ISM/GDP.

tradable_edge: Long ES overnight (16:00 close → 08:30/10:00 ET release) before NFP, ISM and GDP release days; stronger when uncertainty is high.
angles: Overnight long before NFP/ISM/GDP; condition on high pre-release volatility

decay_risk.reason: Published 2022; related FOMC drift faded with low VIX.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Abstract only; needs a macro release calendar (NFP first Friday, ISM 1st business day, GDP advance).
Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
